reading.body:
This record is a single OpenStreetMap node in Italy tagged as a data center, with no megawatts, no operator, and no confirmed business behind it.

The only substantive facts are a name, iZOOM.it, a coordinate near Parma, and an OpenStreetMap tag of telecom=data_center. The name follows a common Italian pattern for hosting and domain businesses, which makes a small web-hosting operation plausible. Nothing in the record establishes that a data center exists at this location, and the research note states that no operator website or Italian business registration was confirmed.

For AI infrastructure, the distinction matters. A tagged node with zero megawatts and no operator is not evidence of compute capacity. The facilities that constrain or supply AI scaling are defined by power contracts, interconnection, and published capacity, none of which appear here. Treating an unverified map tag as a data center would inflate any count of Italian or European capacity.

What this does not tell the reader is the scale, the service offering, or the operating status of iZOOM.it, and it does not tell whether the tag reflects a server room, an office, or an error. The record is filed as plausible and pending, and the research status is exhausted, so the absence of confirmation is a limit of the search session rather than a finding about the site.
